summary: Senior Software Engineer and technical leader with 5+ years of software engineering experience spanning application architecture, full-stack development, enterprise integration, and data engineering. Independently designed and implemented PBK's initial centralized enterprise data foundation in Microsoft Fabric. Previously owned frontend architecture for two customer-facing life insurance applications at State Farm and supported a six-engineer team through design and delivery.
pbk: Independently designed and implemented the initial centralized enterprise data foundation, addressing a longstanding need to consolidate disparate business data. Built Microsoft Fabric ingestion pipelines integrating enterprise systems through APIs and ODBC connections.
Designed and implemented a Bronze/Silver/Gold medallion architecture separating raw ingestion, cleansing and transformation, and curated business data to support reuse and maintainability.

Implemented schema and required-field validation, null handling, normalization, deduplication, record-count checks, and reconciliation. Supported full and incremental ingestion with upsert/merge operations and idempotent execution.

Implemented dependency-based orchestration, retries, timeout and partial failure handling, and manual and independent reprocessing. Preserved historical raw data and supported reprocessing from Bronze.
Implemented pipeline monitoring, execution logging, operational reporting, and automated success and failure email notifications to provide visibility into pipeline health.
Design across applications, services, APIs, storage, and data platforms. Partner with business stakeholders, IT, and development teams to define boundaries, data flows, and dependencies.
Develop an AI-assisted document review workflow to identify missing project data and produce completeness ratings that help prioritize follow-up. Work is ongoing.
Review applications, guide technical handoffs, and establish shared practices for code quality, documentation, maintainability, and ongoing ownership.

stateFarm.title: Architecture, modernization & product delivery
items: Owned frontend architecture and technical direction for two customer-facing life insurance applications built with React, TypeScript, and Redux. Guided delivery across application, API, orchestration, and downstream-service boundaries.
Established reusable state-management and delivery patterns and a shared library of roughly 40 common modules spanning more than 90 source and test files, reducing duplicated state and logic.
Led migration from a retiring UI framework to the enterprise design system, coordinating TypeScript adoption, shared components, testing, and delivery sequencing while product development continued.
Coordinated transaction and reporting workflows across engineering, data, analytics, and business teams. Traced business-event flows and ACORD XML fields to resolve cross-system blockers.

stateFarm.title: Quality, security & production readiness
items: Expanded the primary application's automated suite to 3,335 test cases at 97.08% coverage. Established six CI quality gates with Playwright and Axe browser and accessibility validation.

Redesigned multistage Docker builds and nginx runtime packaging, excluding more than 600 MB of build-time dependencies from final images across both applications; delivered through Red Hat OpenShift on AWS.
Remediated 10 vulnerability findings spanning five CVEs, including seven Critical-severity findings, with eight closed within SLA.
Automated 15-minute deployment visibility for six applications across four shared test environments, completing 100 successful scheduled validation runs.

stateFarm.title: Technical leadership & AI-assisted engineering
items: Supported a six-engineer team through technical design, code reviews, pairing, documentation, stakeholder demos, and candidate interviews; mentored an engineer directly.

Created a 45-page engineering knowledge base covering onboarding, application inventory, testing, environments, and on-call support. Built reusable patterns that other engineers independently extended.
Used AI-assisted programming for implementation, refactoring, testing, documentation, and technical exploration while retaining human review and architectural ownership.

planner: Designed and built an authenticated household cash-flow application with workspace isolation, database-backed sessions, CSRF protection, Flyway migrations, and explicit version-checked saves. Verified with Vitest, Playwright, PostgreSQL integration tests, JaCoCo, and accessibility checks. Local-first; not production hosted.
dsa: Designed and built a framework-free learning application with 55 lessons across 20 topics. Deterministic traces synchronize visualization, source highlighting, narration, and accessible playback. Includes algorithm comparisons, device-local progress, and Node.js, Playwright, and axe-core verification.
